operations.name: list_agent_knowledge_bases
operations.description: Lists knowledge bases associated with an agent and information about each one.

operations.name: list_agent_versions
operations.description: Lists the versions of an agent and information about each version.

operations.name: list_agents
operations.description: Lists the agents belonging to an account and information about each agent.

operations.name: list_data_sources
operations.description: Lists the data sources in a knowledge base and information about each one.

operations.name: list_flow_aliases
operations.description: Returns a list of aliases for a flow.

operations.name: list_flow_versions
operations.description: Returns a list of information about each flow. For more information, see Deploy a flow in Amazon Bedrock in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

operations.name: list_flows
operations.description: Returns a list of flows and information about each flow. For more information, see Manage a flow in Amazon Bedrock in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

operations.name: list_ingestion_jobs
operations.description: Lists the data ingestion jobs for a data source. The list also includes information about each job.

operations.name: list_knowledge_base_documents
operations.description: Retrieves all the documents contained in a data source that is connected to a knowledge base. For more information, see Ingest changes directly into a knowledge base in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

operations.name: list_knowledge_bases
operations.description: Lists the knowledge bases in an account. The list also includesinformation about each knowledge base.

operations.name: list_prompts
operations.description: Returns either information about the working draft (DRAFT version) of each prompt in an account, or information about of all versions of a prompt, depending on whether you include the promptIdentifier field or not. For more information, see View information about prompts using Prompt management in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

operations.name: list_retrieval_instruction_versions
operations.description: Lists the numbered versions of a retrieval instruction, newest first. DRAFT is not listed; read it with GetRetrievalInstruction without retrievalInstructionVersion. Results are paginated. Use the nextToken parameter to retrieve additional results.

operations.name: list_retrieval_instructions
operations.description: Lists the retrieval instructions in the caller's account. Results are paginated. Use the nextToken parameter to retrieve additional results.

operations.name: list_tags_for_resource
operations.description: List all the tags for the resource you specify.

operations.name: list_vpc_configurations
operations.description: Returns a paginated list of the VPC configurations for a knowledge base. You can optionally filter by status. Use the nextToken parameter to retrieve additional results.

operations.name: prepare_agent
operations.description: Creates a DRAFT version of the agent that can be used for internal testing.

operations.name: prepare_flow
operations.description: Prepares the DRAFT version of a flow so that it can be invoked. For more information, see Test a flow in Amazon Bedrock in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

operations.name: put_resource_policy
operations.description: Associates a resource policy with a knowledge base. A resource policy allows other AWS accounts to access the knowledge base. For more information, see Cross-account access for knowledge bases.

operations.name: start_ingestion_job
operations.description: Begins a data ingestion job. Data sources are ingested into your knowledge base so that Large Language Models (LLMs) can use your data.

operations.name: stop_ingestion_job
operations.description: Stops a currently running data ingestion job. You can send a StartIngestionJob request again to ingest the rest of your data when you are ready.

operations.name: tag_resource
operations.description: Associate tags with a resource. For more information, see Tagging resources in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

operations.name: untag_resource
operations.description: Remove tags from a resource.

operations.name: update_agent
operations.description: Updates the configuration of an agent.

operations.name: update_agent_action_group
operations.description: Updates the configuration for an action group for an agent.

operations.name: update_agent_alias
operations.description: Updates configurations for an alias of an agent.

operations.name: update_agent_collaborator
operations.description: Updates an agent's collaborator.

operations.name: update_agent_knowledge_base
operations.description: Updates the configuration for a knowledge base that has been associated with an agent.

operations.name: update_data_source
operations.description: Updates the configurations for a data source connector.  You can't change the chunkingConfiguration after you create the data source connector. Specify the existing chunkingConfiguration.

operations.name: update_flow
operations.description: Modifies a flow. Include both fields that you want to keep and fields that you want to change. For more information, see How it works and Create a flow in Amazon Bedrock in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

operations.name: update_flow_alias
operations.description: Modifies the alias of a flow. Include both fields that you want to keep and ones that you want to change. For more information, see Deploy a flow in Amazon Bedrock in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

operations.name: update_knowledge_base
operations.description: Updates the configuration of a knowledge base with the fields that you specify. Because all fields will be overwritten, you must include the same values for fields that you want to keep the same. You can change the following fields:    name     description     roleArn    You can't change the knowledgeBaseConfiguration or storageConfiguration fields, so you must specify the same configurations as when you created the knowledge base. You can send a GetKnowledgeBase request and copy the same configurations.

operations.name: update_prompt
operations.description: Modifies a prompt in your prompt library. Include both fields that you want to keep and fields that you want to replace. For more information, see Prompt management in Amazon Bedrock and Edit prompts in your prompt library in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

operations.name: update_retrieval_instruction
operations.description: Updates the content of a retrieval instruction. The update is processed asynchronously; the stored content is a candidate until content review passes, and the served content does not change while the update is in flight. The service rejects the request with ConflictException while lastTransitionStatus is CREATING or UPDATING.

operations.name: validate_flow_definition
operations.description: Validates the definition of a flow.

operations.name: agentic_retrieve_stream
operations.description: Retrieves information from one or more knowledge bases using an agentic approach. Agentic retrieval uses a foundation model to intelligently decompose complex queries into sub-queries and iteratively retrieve relevant information from your knowledge bases. This approach improves retrieval accuracy for complex, multi-step questions that a single retrieval pass might not fully address. The operation returns results through a stream that includes retrieval results, trace events for visibility into the process, and a generated response synthesized from the results by default, which can be turned off.

operations.name: check_ingested_document_acl
operations.description: Checks whether a user has access to a specific document by verifying against the ingested access control list (ACL) in a knowledge base. Use this operation to validate that document-level access control is working as expected after ingestion. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock:CheckIngestedDocumentAcl permission.

operations.name: create_invocation
operations.description: Creates a new invocation within a session. An invocation groups the related invocation steps that store the content from a conversation. For more information about sessions, see Store and retrieve conversation history and context with Amazon Bedrock sessions. Related APIs    ListInvocations     ListSessions     GetSession

operations.name: create_session
operations.description: Creates a session to temporarily store conversations for generative AI (GenAI) applications built with open-source frameworks such as LangGraph and LlamaIndex. Sessions enable you to save the state of conversations at checkpoints, with the added security and infrastructure of Amazon Web Services. For more information, see Store and retrieve conversation history and context with Amazon Bedrock sessions. By default, Amazon Bedrock uses Amazon Web Services-managed keys for session encryption, including session metadata, or you can use your own KMS key. For more information, see Amazon Bedrock session encryption.   You use a session to store state and conversation history for generative AI applications built with open-source frameworks. For Amazon Bedrock Agents, the service automatically manages conversation context and associates them with the agent-specific sessionId you specify in the InvokeAgent API operation.   Related APIs:    ListSessions     GetSession     EndSession     DeleteSes

operations.name: delete_agent_memory
operations.description: Deletes memory from the specified memory identifier.

operations.name: delete_session
operations.description: Deletes a session that you ended. You can't delete a session with an ACTIVE status. To delete an active session, you must first end it with the EndSession API operation. For more information about sessions, see Store and retrieve conversation history and context with Amazon Bedrock sessions.

operations.name: end_session
operations.description: Ends the session. After you end a session, you can still access its content but you can’t add to it. To delete the session and it's content, you use the DeleteSession API operation. For more information about sessions, see Store and retrieve conversation history and context with Amazon Bedrock sessions.

operations.name: generate_query
operations.description: Generates an SQL query from a natural language query. For more information, see Generate a query for structured data in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

operations.name: get_agent_memory
operations.description: Gets the sessions stored in the memory of the agent.

operations.name: get_document_content
operations.description: Retrieves the content of an ingested document from a knowledge base. Returns a pre-signed URL for secure document access.

operations.name: get_execution_flow_snapshot
operations.description: Retrieves the flow definition snapshot used for a flow execution. The snapshot represents the flow metadata and definition as it existed at the time the execution was started. Note that even if the flow is edited after an execution starts, the snapshot connected to the execution remains unchanged.  Flow executions is in preview release for Amazon Bedrock and is subject to change.

operations.name: get_flow_execution
operations.description: Retrieves details about a specific flow execution, including its status, start and end times, and any errors that occurred during execution.

operations.name: get_ingested_document_acl
operations.description: Retrieves the ingested access control list (ACL) for a specific document in a knowledge base. Use this operation to inspect the allow and deny lists that were ingested for a document to troubleshoot access control issues. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock:GetIngestedDocumentAcl permission.

operations.name: get_invocation_step
operations.description: Retrieves the details of a specific invocation step within an invocation in a session. For more information about sessions, see Store and retrieve conversation history and context with Amazon Bedrock sessions.

operations.name: get_session
operations.description: Retrieves details about a specific session. For more information about sessions, see Store and retrieve conversation history and context with Amazon Bedrock sessions.

operations.name: invoke_agent
operations.description: Amazon Bedrock Agents (now Amazon Bedrock Agents Classic) is no longer open to new customers. For capabilities similar to Bedrock Agents Classic, explore Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Existing customers can continue to use the service as normal. For more information, see Amazon Bedrock Agents Classic availability change.    Sends a prompt for the agent to process and respond to. Note the following fields for the request:   To continue the same conversation with an agent, use the same sessionId value in the request.   To activate trace enablement, turn enableTrace to true. Trace enablement helps you follow the agent's reasoning process that led it to the information it processed, the actions it took, and the final result it yielded. For more information, see Trace enablement.   End a conversation by setting endSession to true.   In the sessionState object, you can include attributes for the session or prompt or, if you configured an action group to return control, results from invocation of

operations.name: invoke_flow
operations.description: Invokes an alias of a flow to run the inputs that you specify and return the output of each node as a stream. If there's an error, the error is returned. For more information, see Test a flow in Amazon Bedrock in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.  The CLI doesn't support streaming operations in Amazon Bedrock, including InvokeFlow.

operations.name: invoke_inline_agent
operations.description: Invokes an inline Amazon Bedrock agent using the configurations you provide with the request.    Specify the following fields for security purposes.   (Optional) customerEncryptionKeyArn – The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a KMS key to encrypt the creation of the agent.   (Optional) idleSessionTTLinSeconds – Specify the number of seconds for which the agent should maintain session information. After this time expires, the subsequent InvokeInlineAgent request begins a new session.     To override the default prompt behavior for agent orchestration and to use advanced prompts, include a promptOverrideConfiguration object. For more information, see Advanced prompts.   The agent instructions will not be honored if your agent has only one knowledge base, uses default prompts, has no action group, and user input is disabled.

operations.name: list_flow_execution_events
operations.description: Lists events that occurred during a flow execution. Events provide detailed information about the execution progress, including node inputs and outputs, flow inputs and outputs, condition results, and failure events.  Flow executions is in preview release for Amazon Bedrock and is subject to change.

operations.name: list_flow_executions
operations.description: Lists all executions of a flow. Results can be paginated and include summary information about each execution, such as status, start and end times, and the execution's Amazon Resource Name (ARN).  Flow executions is in preview release for Amazon Bedrock and is subject to change.

operations.name: list_invocation_steps
operations.description: Lists all invocation steps associated with a session and optionally, an invocation within the session. For more information about sessions, see Store and retrieve conversation history and context with Amazon Bedrock sessions.

operations.name: list_invocations
operations.description: Lists all invocations associated with a specific session. For more information about sessions, see Store and retrieve conversation history and context with Amazon Bedrock sessions.

operations.name: list_sessions
operations.description: Lists all sessions in your Amazon Web Services account. For more information about sessions, see Store and retrieve conversation history and context with Amazon Bedrock sessions.

operations.name: list_tags_for_resource
operations.description: List all the tags for the resource you specify.

operations.name: optimize_prompt
operations.description: Optimizes a prompt for the task that you specify. For more information, see Optimize a prompt in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

operations.name: put_invocation_step
operations.description: Add an invocation step to an invocation in a session. An invocation step stores fine-grained state checkpoints, including text and images, for each interaction. For more information about sessions, see Store and retrieve conversation history and context with Amazon Bedrock sessions. Related APIs:    GetInvocationStep     ListInvocationSteps     ListInvocations     ListSessions

operations.name: rerank
operations.description: Reranks the relevance of sources based on queries. For more information, see Improve the relevance of query responses with a reranker model.

operations.name: retrieve
operations.description: Queries a knowledge base and retrieves information from it.

operations.name: retrieve_and_generate
operations.description: Queries a knowledge base and generates responses based on the retrieved results and using the specified foundation model or inference profile. The response only cites sources that are relevant to the query.  This API cannot be used with managed knowledge bases. Use AgenticRetrieveStream or Retrieve with managed knowledge bases.

operations.name: retrieve_and_generate_stream
operations.description: Queries a knowledge base and generates responses based on the retrieved results, with output in streaming format.  This API cannot be used with managed knowledge bases. Use AgenticRetrieveStream or Retrieve with managed knowledge bases.   The CLI doesn't support streaming operations in Amazon Bedrock, including InvokeModelWithResponseStream.  This operation requires permission for the  bedrock:RetrieveAndGenerate action.

operations.name: start_flow_execution
operations.description: Starts an execution of an Amazon Bedrock flow. Unlike flows that run until completion or time out after five minutes, flow executions let you run flows asynchronously for longer durations. Flow executions also yield control so that your application can perform other tasks. This operation returns an Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that you can use to track and manage your flow execution.  Flow executions is in preview release for Amazon Bedrock and is subject to change.

operations.name: stop_flow_execution
operations.description: Stops an Amazon Bedrock flow's execution. This operation prevents further processing of the flow and changes the execution status to Aborted.

operations.name: tag_resource
operations.description: Associate tags with a resource. For more information, see Tagging resources in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

operations.name: untag_resource
operations.description: Remove tags from a resource.

operations.name: update_session
operations.description: Updates the metadata or encryption settings of a session. For more information about sessions, see Store and retrieve conversation history and context with Amazon Bedrock sessions.

operations.name: batch_create_memory_records
operations.description: Creates multiple memory records in a single batch operation for the specified memory with custom content.

operations.name: batch_delete_memory_records
operations.description: Deletes multiple memory records in a single batch operation from the specified memory.

operations.name: batch_update_memory_records
operations.description: Updates multiple memory records with custom content in a single batch operation within the specified memory.

operations.name: complete_resource_token_auth
operations.description: Confirms the user authentication session for obtaining OAuth2.0 tokens for a resource.

operations.name: create_ab_test
operations.description: Creates an A/B test for comparing agent configurations. A/B tests split traffic between a control variant and a treatment variant through a gateway, then evaluate performance using online evaluation configurations to determine which variant performs better.

operations.name: create_event
operations.description: Creates an event in an AgentCore Memory resource. Events represent interactions or activities that occur within a session and are associated with specific actors. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:CreateEvent permission. This operation is subject to request rate limiting.

operations.name: create_payment_instrument
operations.description: Create a new payment instrument for a connector.

operations.name: create_payment_session
operations.description: Create a new payment session.

operations.name: delete_ab_test
operations.description: Deletes an A/B test and its associated gateway rules.

operations.name: delete_batch_evaluation
operations.description: Deletes a batch evaluation and its associated results.

operations.name: delete_capacity_provider_session
operations.description: Deletes a session associated with a capacity provider in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and makes the session unavailable for further use. To delete a capacity provider session, specify both the capacity provider identifier and the session ID. After you delete a session, you cannot restart it.

operations.name: delete_event
operations.description: Deletes an event from an AgentCore Memory resource. When you delete an event, it is permanently removed. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:DeleteEvent permission.

operations.name: delete_memory_record
operations.description: Deletes a memory record from an AgentCore Memory resource. When you delete a memory record, it is permanently removed. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:DeleteMemoryRecord permission.

operations.name: delete_payment_instrument
operations.description: Deletes a payment instrument. This is a soft delete operation that preserves the record for audit and compliance purposes.

operations.name: delete_payment_session
operations.description: Deletes a payment session. This permanently removes the payment session record.

operations.name: delete_recommendation
operations.description: Deletes a recommendation and its associated results.

operations.name: evaluate
operations.description: Performs on-demand evaluation of agent traces using a specified evaluator. This synchronous API accepts traces in OpenTelemetry format and returns immediate scoring results with detailed explanations.

operations.name: get_ab_test
operations.description: Retrieves detailed information about an A/B test, including its configuration, status, and statistical results.

operations.name: get_agent_card
operations.description: Retrieves the A2A agent card associated with an AgentCore Runtime agent.

operations.name: get_batch_evaluation
operations.description: Retrieves detailed information about a batch evaluation, including its status, configuration, results, and any error details.

operations.name: get_browser_session
operations.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific browser session in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This operation returns the session's configuration, current status, associated streams, and metadata. To get a browser session, you must specify both the browser identifier and the session ID. The response includes information about the session's viewport configuration, timeout settings, and stream endpoints. The following operations are related to GetBrowserSession:    StartBrowserSession     ListBrowserSessions     StopBrowserSession

operations.name: get_code_interpreter_session
operations.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific code interpreter session in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This operation returns the session's configuration, current status, and metadata. To get a code interpreter session, you must specify both the code interpreter identifier and the session ID. The response includes information about the session's timeout settings and current status. The following operations are related to GetCodeInterpreterSession:    StartCodeInterpreterSession     ListCodeInterpreterSessions     StopCodeInterpreterSession

operations.name: get_event
operations.description: Retrieves information about a specific event in an AgentCore Memory resource. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:GetEvent permission.

operations.name: get_memory_record
operations.description: Retrieves a specific memory record from an AgentCore Memory resource. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:GetMemoryRecord permission.

operations.name: get_payment_instrument
operations.description: Get a payment instrument by ID.

operations.name: get_payment_instrument_balance
operations.description: Get the balance of a payment instrument.

operations.name: get_payment_session
operations.description: Get a payment session.

operations.name: get_recommendation
operations.description: Retrieves detailed information about a recommendation, including its configuration, status, and results.

operations.name: get_resource_api_key
operations.description: Retrieves the API key associated with an API key credential provider.

operations.name: get_resource_oauth2_token
operations.description: Returns the OAuth 2.0 token of the provided resource.

operations.name: get_resource_payment_token
operations.description: Generates authentication tokens for payment providers that use vendor-specific authentication mechanisms.

operations.name: get_workload_access_token
operations.description: Obtains a workload access token for agentic workloads not acting on behalf of a user.

operations.name: get_workload_access_token_for_jwt
operations.description: Obtains a workload access token for agentic workloads acting on behalf of a user, using a JWT token.

operations.name: get_workload_access_token_for_user_id
operations.description: Obtains a workload access token for agentic workloads acting on behalf of a user, using the user's ID.

operations.name: ingest_data
operations.description: Submits content directly for ingestion to generate long-term memory records in a AgentCore Memory resource. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:IngestData permission.

operations.name: invoke_agent_runtime
operations.description: Sends a request to an agent or tool hosted in an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and receives responses in real-time.  To invoke an agent, you can specify either the AgentCore Runtime ARN or the agent ID with an account ID, and provide a payload containing your request. When you use the agent ID instead of the full ARN, you don't need to URL-encode the identifier. You can optionally specify a qualifier to target a specific endpoint of the agent. This operation supports streaming responses, allowing you to receive partial responses as they become available. We recommend using pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully when processing large responses. For example code, see Invoke an AgentCore Runtime agent.  If you're integrating your agent with OAuth, you can't use the Amazon Web Services SDK to call InvokeAgentRuntime. Instead, make a HTTPS request to InvokeAgentRuntime. For an example, see Authenticate and authorize with Inbound Auth and Outbound Auth. T

operations.name: invoke_agent_runtime_command
operations.description: Executes a command in a runtime session container and streams the output back to the caller. This operation allows you to run shell commands within the agent runtime environment and receive real-time streaming responses including standard output and standard error. To invoke a command, you must specify the agent runtime ARN and a runtime session ID. The command execution supports streaming responses, allowing you to receive output as it becomes available through contentStart, contentDelta, and contentStop events. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand permission.

operations.name: invoke_browser
operations.description: Invokes an operating system-level action on a browser session in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This operation provides direct OS-level control over browser sessions, enabling mouse actions, keyboard input, and screenshots that the WebSocket-based Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) cannot handle — such as interacting with print dialogs, context menus, and JavaScript alerts. You send a request with exactly one action in the BrowserAction union, and receive a corresponding result in the BrowserActionResult union. The following operations are related to InvokeBrowser:    StartBrowserSession     GetBrowserSession     StopBrowserSession

operations.name: invoke_code_interpreter
operations.description: Executes code within an active code interpreter session in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This operation processes the provided code, runs it in a secure environment, and returns the execution results including output, errors, and generated visualizations. To execute code, you must specify the code interpreter identifier, session ID, and the code to run in the arguments parameter. The operation returns a stream containing the execution results, which can include text output, error messages, and data visualizations. This operation is subject to request rate limiting based on your account's service quotas. The following operations are related to InvokeCodeInterpreter:    StartCodeInterpreterSession     GetCodeInterpreterSession

operations.name: invoke_harness
operations.description: Operation to invoke a Harness.

operations.name: list_ab_tests
operations.description: Lists all A/B tests in the account.

operations.name: list_actors
operations.description: Lists all actors in an AgentCore Memory resource. We recommend using pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:ListActors permission.

operations.name: list_batch_evaluations
operations.description: Lists all batch evaluations in the account, providing summary information about each evaluation's status and configuration.

operations.name: list_browser_sessions
operations.description: Retrieves a list of browser sessions in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that match the specified criteria. This operation returns summary information about each session, including identifiers, status, and timestamps. You can filter the results by browser identifier and session status. The operation supports pagination to handle large result sets efficiently. We recommend using pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully when retrieving large numbers of sessions. The following operations are related to ListBrowserSessions:    StartBrowserSession     GetBrowserSession

operations.name: list_code_interpreter_sessions
operations.description: Retrieves a list of code interpreter sessions in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that match the specified criteria. This operation returns summary information about each session, including identifiers, status, and timestamps. You can filter the results by code interpreter identifier and session status. The operation supports pagination to handle large result sets efficiently. We recommend using pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully when retrieving large numbers of sessions. The following operations are related to ListCodeInterpreterSessions:    StartCodeInterpreterSession     GetCodeInterpreterSession

operations.name: list_events
operations.description: Lists events in an AgentCore Memory resource based on specified criteria. We recommend using pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:ListEvents permission.

operations.name: list_memory_extraction_jobs
operations.description: Lists all long-term memory extraction jobs that are eligible to be started with optional filtering. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:ListMemoryExtractionJobs permission.

operations.name: list_memory_records
operations.description: Lists memory records in an AgentCore Memory resource based on specified criteria. We recommend using pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:ListMemoryRecords permission.

operations.name: list_payment_instruments
operations.description: List payment instruments for a manager.

operations.name: list_payment_sessions
operations.description: List payment sessions.

operations.name: list_recommendations
operations.description: Lists all recommendations in the account, with optional filtering by status.

operations.name: list_sessions
operations.description: Lists sessions in an AgentCore Memory resource based on specified criteria. We recommend using pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully. Empty sessions are automatically deleted after one day. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:ListSessions permission.

operations.name: process_payment
operations.description: Processes a payment using a payment instrument within a payment session.

operations.name: retrieve_memory_records
operations.description: Searches for and retrieves memory records from an AgentCore Memory resource based on specified search criteria. We recommend using pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully. To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:RetrieveMemoryRecords permission.

operations.name: save_browser_session_profile
operations.description: Saves the current state of a browser session as a reusable profile in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. A browser profile captures persistent browser data such as cookies and local storage from an active session, enabling you to reuse this data in future browser sessions. To save a browser session profile, you must specify the profile identifier, browser identifier, and session ID. The session must be active when saving the profile. Once saved, the profile can be used with the StartBrowserSession operation to initialize new sessions with the stored browser state. Browser profiles are useful for scenarios that require persistent authentication, maintaining user preferences across sessions, or continuing tasks that depend on previously stored browser data. The following operations are related to SaveBrowserSessionProfile:    StartBrowserSession     GetBrowserSession

operations.name: search_registry_records
operations.description: Searches for registry records using semantic, lexical, or hybrid queries. Returns metadata for matching records ordered by relevance within the specified registry.

operations.name: start_batch_evaluation
operations.description: Starts a batch evaluation job that evaluates agent performance across multiple sessions. Batch evaluations pull agent traces from CloudWatch Logs or an existing online evaluation configuration and run specified evaluators and insights against them.

operations.name: start_browser_session
operations.description: Creates and initializes a browser session in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The session enables agents to navigate and interact with web content, extract information from websites, and perform web-based tasks as part of their response generation. To create a session, you must specify a browser identifier and a name. You can also configure the viewport dimensions to control the visible area of web content. The session remains active until it times out or you explicitly stop it using the StopBrowserSession operation. The following operations are related to StartBrowserSession:    GetBrowserSession     UpdateBrowserStream     SaveBrowserSessionProfile     StopBrowserSession     InvokeBrowser

operations.name: start_code_interpreter_session
operations.description: Creates and initializes a code interpreter session in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The session enables agents to execute code as part of their response generation, supporting programming languages such as Python for data analysis, visualization, and computation tasks. To create a session, you must specify a code interpreter identifier and a name. The session remains active until it times out or you explicitly stop it using the StopCodeInterpreterSession operation. The following operations are related to StartCodeInterpreterSession:    InvokeCodeInterpreter     GetCodeInterpreterSession     StopCodeInterpreterSession

operations.name: start_memory_extraction_job
operations.description: Starts a memory extraction job that processes events that failed extraction previously in an AgentCore Memory resource and produces structured memory records. When earlier extraction attempts have left events unprocessed, this job will pick up and extract those as well.  To use this operation, you must have the bedrock-agentcore:StartMemoryExtractionJob permission.

operations.name: start_recommendation
operations.description: Starts a recommendation job that analyzes agent traces and generates optimization suggestions for system prompts or tool descriptions to improve agent performance.

operations.name: stop_batch_evaluation
operations.description: Stops a running batch evaluation. Sessions that have already been evaluated retain their results.

operations.name: stop_browser_session
operations.description: Terminates an active browser session in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This operation stops the session, releases associated resources, and makes the session unavailable for further use. To stop a browser session, you must specify both the browser identifier and the session ID. Once stopped, a session cannot be restarted; you must create a new session using StartBrowserSession. The following operations are related to StopBrowserSession:    StartBrowserSession     GetBrowserSession

operations.name: stop_code_interpreter_session
operations.description: Terminates an active code interpreter session in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This operation stops the session, releases associated resources, and makes the session unavailable for further use. To stop a code interpreter session, you must specify both the code interpreter identifier and the session ID. Once stopped, a session cannot be restarted; you must create a new session using StartCodeInterpreterSession. The following operations are related to StopCodeInterpreterSession:    StartCodeInterpreterSession     GetCodeInterpreterSession

operations.name: stop_runtime_session
operations.description: Stops a session that is running in an running AgentCore Runtime agent.

operations.name: update_ab_test
operations.description: Updates an A/B test's configuration, including variants, traffic allocation, evaluation settings, or execution status.

operations.name: update_browser_stream
operations.description: Updates a browser stream. To use this operation, you must have permissions to perform the bedrock:UpdateBrowserStream action.

operations.name: add_dataset_examples
operations.description: Adds examples to the dataset's DRAFT. All examples are validated against the dataset's schema type before any writes occur. If any example fails validation, the entire batch is rejected (all-or-nothing semantics).

operations.name: batch_put_gateway_rate_limits
operations.description: Atomically creates or updates multiple rate limits for a gateway. The operation updates existing limits with matching keys and creates new limits for new keys. If the operation fails, the service applies no changes. Retry the request after resolving the issue.

operations.name: create_agent_runtime
operations.description: Creates an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime.

operations.name: create_agent_runtime_endpoint
operations.description: Creates an AgentCore Runtime endpoint.

operations.name: create_api_key_credential_provider
operations.description: Creates a new API key credential provider.

operations.name: create_browser
operations.description: Creates a custom browser.

operations.name: create_browser_profile
operations.description: Creates a browser profile in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. A browser profile stores persistent browser data such as cookies, local storage, session storage, and browsing history that can be saved from browser sessions and reused in subsequent sessions.

operations.name: create_capacity_provider
operations.description: Creates a capacity provider. A capacity provider defines the Amazon EC2 infrastructure for AgentCore Runtime, including the operating system, allowed instance types, networking, and storage. It also specifies the IAM permissions that AgentCore uses to manage those instances. The capacity provider name must be unique within your account. After you create the capacity provider, it enters a CREATING state and transitions to READY when it is available for use.

operations.name: create_code_interpreter
operations.description: Creates a custom code interpreter.

operations.name: create_configuration_bundle
operations.description: Creates a new configuration bundle resource. A configuration bundle stores versioned component configurations for agent evaluation workflows.

operations.name: create_consent_portal
operations.description: Creates a new consent portal.

operations.name: create_dataset
operations.description: Creates a new dataset resource asynchronously. Returns immediately with status CREATING. Poll GetDataset until status transitions to ACTIVE or CREATE_FAILED.

operations.name: create_dataset_version
operations.description: Publishes the current DRAFT as a new numbered version. The DRAFT is preserved and remains editable after publishing. Returns immediately with status UPDATING. Poll GetDataset until status transitions to ACTIVE or UPDATE_FAILED.

operations.name: create_evaluator
operations.description: Creates a custom evaluator for agent quality assessment. Custom evaluators can use either LLM-as-a-Judge configurations with user-defined prompts, rating scales, and model settings, or code-based configurations with customer-managed Lambda functions to evaluate agent performance at tool call, trace, or session levels.

operations.name: create_gateway
operations.description: Creates a gateway for Amazon Bedrock Agent. A gateway serves as an integration point between your agent and external services. If you specify CUSTOM_JWT as the authorizerType, you must provide an authorizerConfiguration.

operations.name: create_gateway_rate_limit
operations.description: Creates a rate limit for a gateway. Rate limits define throttling rules for each dimension that control request rates, token consumption rates, and concurrent connections through the gateway.

operations.name: create_gateway_rule
operations.description: Creates a rule for a gateway. Rules define conditions and actions that control how requests are routed and processed through the gateway, including principal-based access control and path-based routing.

operations.name: create_gateway_target
operations.description: Creates a target for a gateway. A target defines an endpoint that the gateway can connect to.

operations.name: create_harness
operations.description: Operation to create a harness.

operations.name: create_harness_endpoint
operations.description: Operation to create a harness endpoint.

operations.name: create_memory
operations.description: Creates a new Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory resource.

operations.name: create_oauth2_credential_provider
operations.description: Creates a new OAuth2 credential provider.

operations.name: create_online_evaluation_config
operations.description: Creates an online evaluation configuration for continuous monitoring of agent performance. Online evaluation automatically samples live traffic from CloudWatch logs at specified rates and applies evaluators to assess agent quality in production.

operations.name: create_payment_connector
operations.description: Creates a new payment connector for a payment manager. A payment connector integrates with a supported payment provider to enable payment processing capabilities.

operations.name: create_payment_credential_provider
operations.description: Creates a new payment credential provider for storing authentication credentials used by payment connectors to communicate with external payment providers.

operations.name: create_payment_manager
operations.description: Creates a new payment manager in your Amazon Web Services account. A payment manager serves as the top-level resource for managing payment processing capabilities, including payment connectors that integrate with supported payment providers. If you specify CUSTOM_JWT as the authorizerType, you must provide an authorizerConfiguration.

operations.name: create_policy
operations.description: Creates a policy within the AgentCore Policy system. Policies provide real-time, deterministic control over agentic interactions with AgentCore Gateway. Using Cedar or Dogwood, you can define fine-grained policies that specify which interactions with Gateway tools are permitted based on input parameters and OAuth claims, ensuring agents operate within defined boundaries and business rules. The policy is validated during creation against the Cedar schema generated from the Gateway's tools' input schemas, which defines the available tools, their parameters, and expected data types. This is an asynchronous operation. Use the GetPolicy operation to poll the status field to track completion. If the new policy is a temporal policy, creating it invalidates the policy engine's active temporal sessions. For more information about temporal policy sessions, see session-based temporal policies. The policy engine returns an HTTP 409 ConflictException to in-flight sessions. To resume, you must start

operations.name: create_policy_engine
operations.description: Creates a new policy engine within the AgentCore Policy system. A policy engine is a collection of policies that evaluates and authorizes agent tool calls. When associated with Gateways (each Gateway can be associated with at most one policy engine, but multiple Gateways can be associated with the same engine), the policy engine intercepts all agent requests and determines whether to allow or deny each action based on the defined policies. This is an asynchronous operation. Use the GetPolicyEngine operation to poll the status field to track completion.

operations.name: create_registry
operations.description: Creates a new registry in your Amazon Web Services account. A registry serves as a centralized catalog for organizing and managing registry records, including MCP servers, A2A agents, agent skills, and custom resource types. If you specify CUSTOM_JWT as the authorizerType, you must provide an authorizerConfiguration.

operations.name: create_registry_record
operations.description: Creates a new registry record within the specified registry. A registry record represents an individual AI resource's metadata in the registry. This could be an MCP server (and associated tools), A2A agent, agent skill, or a custom resource with a custom schema. The record is processed asynchronously and returns HTTP 202 Accepted.

operations.name: create_workload_identity
operations.description: Creates a new workload identity.

operations.name: delete_agent_runtime
operations.description: Deletes an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, or a single version of an AgentCore Runtime when you provide the version qualifier.

operations.name: delete_agent_runtime_endpoint
operations.description: Deletes an AgentCore Runtime endpoint.

operations.name: delete_api_key_credential_provider
operations.description: Deletes an API key credential provider.

operations.name: delete_browser
operations.description: Deletes a custom browser.

operations.name: delete_browser_profile
operations.description: Deletes a browser profile.

operations.name: delete_capacity_provider
operations.description: Deletes a capacity provider. Before you delete a capacity provider, disassociate all agent runtimes and runtime versions that reference it. If any references remain, the operation fails.

operations.name: delete_code_interpreter
operations.description: Deletes a custom code interpreter.

operations.name: delete_configuration_bundle
operations.description: Deletes a configuration bundle and all of its versions.

operations.name: delete_consent_portal
operations.description: Deletes a consent portal.

operations.name: delete_dataset
operations.description: Deletes a dataset version or an entire dataset asynchronously. If datasetVersion is absent, deletes all versions and the dataset record itself. If provided, deletes only that specific version.

operations.name: delete_dataset_examples
operations.description: Deletes specific examples by ID from DRAFT. All example IDs are validated before any deletes occur. If any ID does not exist in DRAFT, the entire batch is rejected (all-or-nothing semantics).

operations.name: delete_evaluator
operations.description: Deletes a custom evaluator. Builtin evaluators cannot be deleted. The evaluator must not be referenced by any active online evaluation configurations.

operations.name: delete_gateway
operations.description: Deletes a gateway.

operations.name: delete_gateway_rate_limit
operations.description: Deletes a gateway rate limit.

operations.name: delete_gateway_rule
operations.description: Deletes a gateway rule.

operations.name: delete_gateway_target
operations.description: Deletes a gateway target. You cannot delete a target that is in a pending authorization state (CREATE_PENDING_AUTH, UPDATE_PENDING_AUTH, or SYNCHRONIZE_PENDING_AUTH). Wait for the authorization to complete or fail before deleting the target.

operations.name: delete_harness
operations.description: Operation to delete a Harness.

operations.name: delete_harness_endpoint
operations.description: Operation to delete a harness endpoint.

operations.name: delete_memory
operations.description: Deletes an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory resource. When you delete a memory resource, it is permanently removed.

operations.name: delete_oauth2_credential_provider
operations.description: Deletes an OAuth2 credential provider.

operations.name: delete_online_evaluation_config
operations.description: Deletes an online evaluation configuration and stops any ongoing evaluation processes associated with it.

operations.name: delete_payment_connector
operations.description: Deletes a payment connector.

operations.name: delete_payment_credential_provider
operations.description: Deletes a payment credential provider and its associated stored credentials.

operations.name: delete_payment_manager
operations.description: Deletes a payment manager. All payment connectors associated with the payment manager must be deleted before the payment manager can be deleted. This operation initiates the deletion process asynchronously.

operations.name: delete_policy
operations.description: Deletes an existing policy from the AgentCore Policy system. Once deleted, the policy can no longer be used for agent behavior control and all references to it become invalid. This is an asynchronous operation. Use the GetPolicy operation to poll the status field to track completion.

operations.name: delete_policy_engine
operations.description: Deletes an existing policy engine from the AgentCore Policy system. The policy engine must not have any associated policies before deletion. Once deleted, the policy engine and all its configurations become unavailable for policy management and evaluation. This is an asynchronous operation. Use the GetPolicyEngine operation to poll the status field to track completion.

operations.name: delete_registry
operations.description: Deletes a registry. The registry must contain zero records before it can be deleted. This operation initiates the deletion process asynchronously.

operations.name: delete_registry_record
operations.description: Deletes a registry record. The record's status transitions to DELETING and the record is removed asynchronously.

operations.name: delete_resource_policy
operations.description: Deletes the resource-based policy for a specified resource.  This feature is currently available only for AgentCore Runtime and Gateway.

operations.name: delete_workload_identity
operations.description: Deletes a workload identity.

operations.name: get_agent_runtime
operations.description: Gets an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime.

operations.name: get_agent_runtime_endpoint
operations.description: Gets information about an Amazon Secure AgentEndpoint.

operations.name: get_api_key_credential_provider
operations.description: Retrieves information about an API key credential provider.

operations.name: get_browser
operations.description: Gets information about a custom browser.

operations.name: get_browser_profile
operations.description: Gets information about a browser profile.

operations.name: get_capacity_provider
operations.description: Retrieves information about a capacity provider, including its status, permissions configuration, and compute configuration.

operations.name: get_code_interpreter
operations.description: Gets information about a custom code interpreter.

operations.name: get_configuration_bundle
operations.description: Gets the latest version of a configuration bundle. By default, returns the latest version on the mainline branch. Use GetConfigurationBundleVersion to retrieve a specific historical version.

operations.name: get_configuration_bundle_version
operations.description: Gets a specific version of a configuration bundle by its version identifier.

operations.name: get_consent_portal
operations.description: Retrieves information about a consent portal.

operations.name: get_dataset
operations.description: Retrieves dataset metadata. Use the datasetVersion query parameter to retrieve a specific version's metadata. If absent, defaults to DRAFT. For paginated example content, use ListDatasetExamples.

operations.name: get_evaluator
operations.description: Retrieves detailed information about an evaluator, including its configuration, status, and metadata. Works with both built-in and custom evaluators.

operations.name: get_gateway
operations.description: Retrieves information about a specific Gateway.

operations.name: get_gateway_rate_limit
operations.description: Retrieves information about a gateway rate limit.

operations.name: get_gateway_rule
operations.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific gateway rule.

operations.name: get_gateway_target
operations.description: Retrieves information about a specific gateway target.

operations.name: get_harness

operations.name: rotate_payment_connector_credentials
operations.description: Replaces the service-managed credentials of a payment connector with newly issued credentials. Use this operation only for payment connectors with a provisionMode of QUICK_CREATE. For payment connectors with a provisionMode of MANUAL, call UpdatePaymentCredentialProvider instead after rotating credentials with the payment provider directly. The rotation finishes before the response is returned, and only one rotation runs at a time for a given payment connector. When it succeeds, the new credential is in effect and the payment connector stays in the READY state. When it fails, an error is returned, the payment connector and its existing credential are left unchanged, and you can retry the request. Rotation replaces the credential on the connector's credential provider, so every payment connector that uses that provider is affected. Replace any copy of the previous credential that you use outside AgentCore.

operations.name: start_policy_generation
operations.description: Initiates the AI-powered generation of Dogwood policies from natural language descriptions within the AgentCore Policy system. This feature enables both technical and non-technical users to create policies by describing their authorization requirements in plain English, which is then automatically translated into formal Dogwood policy statements. The generation process analyzes the natural language input along with the Gateway's tool context to produce validated policy options. Generated policy assets are automatically deleted after 7 days, so you should review and create policies from the generated assets within this timeframe. Once created, policies are permanent and not subject to this expiration. Generated policies should be reviewed and tested in log-only mode before deploying to production. Use this when you want to describe policy intent naturally rather than learning Dogwood syntax, though generated policies may require refinement for complex scenarios.

You cannot synchronize a target that is in a pending authorization state (CREATE_PENDING_AUTH, UPDATE_PENDING_AUTH, or SYNCHRONIZE_PENDING_AUTH). Wait for the authorization to complete or fail before synchronizing. You cannot synchronize a target that has a static tool schema (mcpToolSchema) configured. Remove the static schema through an UpdateGatewayTarget call to enable dynamic tool synchronization.

This feature is currently available only for AgentCore Runtime, Browser, Browser Profile, Code Interpreter tool, and Gateway.

operations.description: Updates an existing policy within the AgentCore Policy system. This operation allows modification of the policy description and definition while maintaining the policy's identity. The updated policy is validated against the Cedar schema before being applied. This is an asynchronous operation. Use the GetPolicy operation to poll the status field to track completion. If the updated policy is a temporal policy, the policy engine invalidates all active temporal sessions. If the update adds or removes temporal operators, the policy engine also invalidates active temporal sessions. For more information about temporal policy sessions, see session-based temporal policies. The policy engine returns an HTTP 409 ConflictException to in-flight sessions. To resume, you must start a new session with a new session ID.

operations.name: count_tokens
operations.description: Returns the token count for a given inference request. This operation helps you estimate token usage before sending requests to foundation models by returning the token count that would be used if the same input were sent to the model in an inference request. Token counting is model-specific because different models use different tokenization strategies. The token count returned by this operation will match the token count that would be charged if the same input were sent to the model in an InvokeModel or Converse request. You can use this operation to:   Estimate costs before sending inference requests.   Optimize prompts to fit within token limits.   Plan for token usage in your applications.   This operation accepts the same input formats as InvokeModel and Converse, allowing you to count tokens for both raw text inputs and structured conversation formats. It is possible for users to interrupt the model's response with a new prompt, which will halt the response speech. The model will retain contextual awareness of the conversation while pivoting to respond to the new prompt.

operations.name: delete_trail
operations.description:
Deletes a trail. This operation must be called from the Region in which the trail was
         created. DeleteTrail cannot be called on the shadow trails (replicated trails
         in other Regions) of a trail that is enabled in all Regions.
         
            
         While deleting a CloudTrail trail is an irreversible action, CloudTrail does not
         delete log files in the Amazon S3 bucket for that trail, the Amazon S3 bucket itself, or the
         CloudWatchlog group to which the trail delivers events. Deleting a multi-Region trail
         will stop logging of events in all Amazon Web Services Regions enabled in your Amazon Web Services account. Deleting a
         single-Region trail will stop logging of events in that Region only. It will not stop
         logging of events in other Regions even if the trails in those other Regions have
         identical names to the deleted trail.

         of results.

         specified time range. The public key is needed to validate digest files that were signed

      have one active (RUNNING or PENDING) export task at a time. To
